userStories.title: Title sessions from the user's typed line
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist the user's typed slash line as a new session's title and share readable title rendering across the resume picker and sessions listing.

**Motivation** — `/resume` listed `<skill name="superpowers:brainstorming" location="/Users/williamkhoo/.claude/plu` as a session title twice, because `writeTurnMeta` (`packages/nax/src/chat/turn-runner.ts`) titles a session from the first message SENT, and a `/skill` turn sends the expanded `buildSkillInvocationMessage` envelope.

**Approach** — Title from the typed line. `ChatHost.send` takes an optional `{ title }`. When the text `ChatApp` sends differs from the line the user typed — a skill, `/feature` or catalog command turn — it passes the typed slash line `/<name><rest>` as `title`; a plain message (and a job delivery) is sent with no options, exactly as today, because the message is its own title. `writeTurnMeta` titles a new session from `title` when present instead of the sent text. A pure `sessionTitleText` renders any stored title for display, so the titles already on disk that hold a skill envelope show as `/<skill name>`.

`ChatHost.send` gains `ChatSendOptions { title? }`, threaded into `runChatTurn` and `writeTurnMeta`. `ChatApp` passes `{ title: "/<name><rest>" }` for a turn produced by a slash command (skill, `/feature`, catalog command) and calls `send` with two arguments for a plain message, as today. New `sessionTitleText` renders a stored title for display (`untitled <first 8 id chars>` for null, `/<name>` for a legacy skill-envelope title, else the title), and the `/resume` picker rows and the `/sessions` listing use it.

`RunChatTurnOptions` adds `readonly title?: string`; `writeTurnMeta` titles from `stored.title ?? clip(options.title?.trim() || message)` (clip = the existing whitespace collapse and 80-code-point cut), so an empty or whitespace-only title falls back to the message.

`sendTurn` inside `ChatApp`: Target: `sendTurn(message, prepare?, title?)`. It calls `host.send(sent, onEvent)` with two arguments when the sent text equals the title it would pass, and `host.send(sent, onEvent, { title })` otherwise, where `title` is the `title` argument or, for a catalog command, the `message` argument (`/<name><rest>`). Preserve the slash parser's raw rest when supplying the title. The equality rule above is authoritative: even a slash-produced turn is sent with exactly two arguments when the payload equals the title candidate. A `/feature` turn's first argument remains buildChatFeatureMessage output; its typed slash line is the third argument's title field, never a replacement message.

Failure handling: `options.title` is absent or the empty string — the title falls back to the sent message, as today. Preserve the existing stored title after subsequent turns. The malformed stored-title fixtures in the acceptance criteria must remain unchanged: preserve both the spec's literal `<skill name="x"` prefix and its stated unterminated-name case `<skill name="x` (no closing quote). Treat this as a narrow clarification of the supplied malformed fixture, not a reason to require a location attribute on every legacy title.

**Scope** — In: modify turn-runner.ts, chat-host.ts, ChatApp.tsx, Picker.tsx, slash-commands.ts and the chat barrel; create session-title.ts. Export `sessionTitleText` and `ChatSendOptions` from the chat barrel so the TUI imports them through it. Update turn-runner.test.ts for title options; the existing AC-15/AC-16 title assertions stay as they are because a send without `title` still titles from the message. Update exact-arity expanded-send assertions in slash-resources.test.tsx, slash-commands.test.tsx and chat-shell-lines.test.tsx to include the typed-line options object; plain-message assertions stay two-argument. Update picker legacy-envelope labels while preserving null-title labels. Out: session history and hygiene (US-002), replay mapping (US-003), transcript rebuilds/header titles (US-004). Collapsing a skill invocation into an expandable row, live or replayed, belongs to the later chat-transcript-polish feature; this feature only replays a skill envelope as its typed `/name args` line.

**Interface**
```typescript
export interface ChatSendOptions { readonly title?: string }
send(message: string, onEvent: (event: SessionEvent) => void, options?: ChatSendOptions): Promise<void>
readonly title?: string; // RunChatTurnOptions
sessionTitleText(title: string | null, sessionId: string): string
```
`session-title.ts` is a new pure module; the optional options parameter is additive and plain sends retain their exact current arity. No persisted legacy-title migration is performed. A stored title is a legacy skill envelope only when it starts with `<skill name="`, the name's closing quote is present, and that quote is followed by whitespace; any other title is shown unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] runChatTurn with message: '<skill …>body' and title: '/brainstorm plan it' on a session whose stored meta has title: null writes meta with title === '/brainstorm plan it'.
[unit] runChatTurn with title: '' and message: 'hello there' writes title === 'hello there'.
[unit] runChatTurn with title longer than 80 code points writes the first 80 code points after collapsing whitespace, the same clip a message gets.
[unit] A second runChatTurn with a different title on a session whose stored meta already has title: 'first' leaves title === 'first'.
[integration] NativeChatHost.send('expanded', onEvent, { title: '/x y' }) on a fresh session results in stored meta title === '/x y'.
[unit] sessionTitleText(null, 'fba63185-0000-4000-8000-000000000000') returns 'untitled fba63185'.
[unit] sessionTitleText('<skill name="superpowers:brainstorming" location="/Users/a/.claude/plu', id) returns '/superpowers:brainstorming'.
[unit] sessionTitleText('fix the login bug', id) returns 'fix the login bug'.

[unit] sessionTitleText(title, id) returns the stored title unchanged for both the spec's literal malformed-title fixture '<skill name="x"' and a title with an unterminated name attribute (no closing quote), '<skill name="x'.
[integration] Typing hello world and Return in a mounted ChatApp calls the host's send with exactly two arguments, 'hello world' and the event callback.
[unit] runChatTurn with title: '   ' and message: 'hello there' writes title === 'hello there'.

[integration] Typing /superpowers:brainstorming plan the cut for a catalog skill calls send with the skill invocation message as the first argument and { title: '/superpowers:brainstorming plan the cut' } as the third.

[integration] Typing /feature chat-resume-sessions with a readable spec calls host.send with the expanded buildChatFeatureMessage payload as its first argument, the event callback as its second, and { title: '/feature chat-resume-sessions' } as its third argument.

[integration] Typing a catalog command /review now calls host.send with the expanded template message as its first argument, the event callback as its second, and { title: '/review now' } as its third argument.
[integration] The /resume picker draws a session row whose stored title is a skill envelope as /superpowers:brainstorming.
[integration] /sessions prints each row as <sessionId> <sessionTitleText(title, sessionId)>, so a null-title row reads <id> untitled <8 id chars>.
[unit] runChatTurn with options.title absent and message: 'hello there' on untitled metadata writes title === 'hello there', as today.

routing.reasoning: Typed-title provenance crosses the UI, host API, turn persistence and multiple display consumers with exact-arity compatibility requirements. Session metadata changes invoke the sessions security override and strict test/implementation isolation.

suggestedCriteria: When a job delivery submits text through mounted ChatApp, host.send receives exactly the message and event callback with no options argument.
When a catalog command expands to exactly its typed slash line, ChatApp calls host.send with exactly two arguments.

modifiedFiles.reason: export `sessionTitleText` and `ChatSendOptions` from the chat barrel so the TUI imports them through it.
add cases for the `title` option; the existing AC-15/AC-16 title assertions stay as they are because a send without `title` still titles from the message.

skill and catalog command sends now carry a third argument, an options object whose title is the typed slash line; exact-arity assertions on those sends (message plus a function matcher) gain that options object. Plain-message send assertions stay two-argument.

skill, feature and catalog command sends now carry a third argument, an options object whose title is the typed slash line; exact-arity assertions on those sends gain that options object. Plain-message send assertions stay two-argument.
catalog command sends now carry a third argument, an options object whose title is the typed slash line; exact-arity assertions on those sends gain that options object.

a resume row for a null title still reads `untitled <8 id chars>`; rows built from a legacy skill-envelope title now read as a slash and the skill name, so any fixture asserting the raw envelope as a label changes to that form.

userStories.title: Filter resumable sessions and expose opening history
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose the opened transcript snapshot and keep current/turnless sessions out of resume listings while conservatively cleaning up empty sessions this host leaves.

**Motivation** — The list's first row was `untitled fba63185  just now`: the session the user was in. Every `nax chat` start writes a meta file (`openChatSession`), so sessions closed without a turn pile up as `untitled <id>` rows.

**Approach** — List hygiene. A session "has had a turn" when its stored meta has a non-null `updatedAt` (`writeTurnMeta` sets it; `openChatSession` writes `updatedAt: null` for a new session). The host's list and its latest-session choice skip sessions without a turn, and the list skips the host's own session. When the host leaves a session (a `replace` to a different id, or `close`) whose stored meta still has `updatedAt === null`, whose handle's `history.messages` was empty, and on which no `send` was attempted, it removes that session's meta after closing its handle, so new empty sessions stop accumulating. The filtering, the sent-on set and the cleanup live entirely in a new `packages/nax/src/chat/session-hygiene.ts`, because `chat-host.ts` is 570 of its 600 allowed lines; the host gains at most 25 net lines, and a measured overage is resolved by moving more code into that module, never by raising the cap.

History on the handle. `openChatSession` keeps the transcript document it already loads and returns its messages and `savedAt` on the handle; `ChatHost.history()` returns them for the current session. It is the snapshot taken when the session was opened, not a live view; the screen reads it only when the session id changes.

`openChatSession` returns the loaded transcript's messages and `savedAt` on the handle, and the host's `history()` returns the current handle's. `listSessions` skips the host's own session (read from `this.handle?.meta.sessionId`, so listing with no open session does not throw) and sessions whose meta has `updatedAt === null`; `latestId` skips the latter too. The host records each session id it attempted a `send` on; when it replaces a session with a different id or closes, it removes the left session's meta after closing its handle if the stored meta still has `updatedAt === null` and the id was never sent on, additionally requiring empty opening history as specified above. A mode or model switch (same id) removes nothing.

`ChatHistory` — declared in `packages/nax/src/chat/open-chat-session.ts` (which `chat-host.ts` already imports, so no new import edge) and re-exported from `packages/nax/src/chat/index.ts`. `ChatSessionHandle` adds an OPTIONAL `readonly history?: ChatHistory` (typed handle fakes in tests build `{ session, meta, release }`); `openChatSession` always sets it — `{ messages: doc.messages, savedAt: doc.savedAt }` when a document was loaded, `{ messages: [] }` otherwise. `ChatHost.history` is new, optional so typed test fakes keep compiling, returning `this.handle?.history ?? { messages: [] }`.

New `packages/nax/src/chat/session-hygiene.ts` — `hasHadTurn(meta: SessionMeta): boolean` (`meta.updatedAt !== null`); `resumableRows(input)` that reads each listed session's meta and drops the host's own id and turnless sessions; `removeIfEmpty(input)` that re-reads the meta and removes it when `updatedAt === null`, the left handle's `history.messages` is empty and the id is not in the host's sent-on set, warning instead of throwing; a re-read that finds no meta (`readMeta` returns `null`) does nothing and logs nothing.

`SessionStorage.readMeta(id)`, `removeMeta(id)`, `list({ cwd, cursor })` (`@nathapp/nax-agent`); a list entry's `updatedAt` falls back to `createdAt`, so it cannot tell a turnless session apart — the meta must be read. Keep all existing pagination, latest mode validation, metadata identity checks, lock-holder exclusion and advisory pid badges. Explicit resume by id is not gated on hasHadTurn. Preserve same-id reopens, rollback, drain/unlock ordering and host teardown error guarantees. The sent-on set belongs to the new hygiene module and survives same-id reopens.

Failure handling: reading one session's meta fails with `SESSION_META_UNREADABLE` during `listSessions` (reachable only through a race, since `storage.list` already skips unreadable files; tests reach it with a `readMeta` stub) — that row is skipped and `logger.warn("chat", "skipping unreadable session metadata", { sessionId })` is logged; other rows still list. `removeMeta` throws, or a test storage fake lacks it, while the host leaves a turnless session — the error is logged with `logger.warn("chat", "could not remove empty session", { sessionId, cause })` and the replace or close continues. The meta re-read while leaving a session returns `null` (already gone) — nothing is removed and nothing is logged.

**Scope** — In: modify open-chat-session.ts, chat-host.ts and chat/index.ts; create session-hygiene.ts and its unit tests. Re-export ChatHistory through the chat barrel. Extend chat-host.test.ts and chat-host-resume.test.ts; change existing AC-5 from the own freshly opened session to a separate session with updatedAt set while preserving the heldByPid:4242 assertion. Update whole-handle comparisons in open-chat-session.test.ts with the history field. Out: typed-title plumbing/display (US-001), mapping stored messages to rows (US-003), screen/header integration (US-004). A session whose first turn failed before its metadata was written keeps `updatedAt: null` and stays hidden from the list; it is still reachable with `/resume <id>`. Deleting turnless sessions already on disk from earlier versions; they are hidden from the list, not removed. Any change to `@nathapp/nax-agent` or `@nathapp/nax-agent-acp`.

**Interface**
```typescript
export interface ChatHistory { readonly messages: readonly TranscriptDoc["messages"][number][]; readonly savedAt?: string }
readonly history?: ChatHistory; // ChatSessionHandle
history?(): ChatHistory; // ChatHost
hasHadTurn(meta: SessionMeta): boolean
```
The module also owns the new `resumableRows(input)` and `removeIfEmpty(input)` helpers and sent-on tracking. NativeChatHost implements history() as `this.handle?.history ?? { messages: [] }`; the optional interface members are compatibility accommodations, not permission to omit history in the real opener.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] openChatSession for a new session returns a handle whose history equals { messages: [] }.

[unit] openChatSession with resumeId of a session whose transcript store returns a document with two messages and savedAt: '2026-10-28T01:00:00.000Z' returns history with those two messages and that savedAt.
[integration] After resume({ id }) of a stored session with a transcript, host.history() returns that transcript's messages.
[integration] listSessions() does not include the host's current session id.
[integration] listSessions() on a host that has not opened a session returns the stored sessions with a recorded turn and does not throw.
[integration] A host that starts a session, switches mode with switchTo({ mode: 'full' }), sends once, and closes keeps that session's meta.
[integration] listSessions() omits a stored session whose meta has updatedAt: null and includes one whose meta has updatedAt set.
[integration] resume({}) skips a newer stored session whose meta has updatedAt: null and opens the newest session with updatedAt set.
[integration] A host that starts a session and then closes without calling send leaves no meta for that session (storage.readMeta(id) returns null).
[integration] A host that starts a session, calls send, and closes keeps that session's meta.
[integration] A host that starts a session and then resumes another removes the first session's meta when nothing was sent on it.
[integration] A host that resumes a session whose meta has updatedAt: null but whose transcript holds messages, then closes without sending, keeps that session's meta.
[integration] A host whose own session's meta was already removed by another process closes without error and without logging a warning.
[integration] When storage.removeMeta rejects during close, close resolves and the logger records warn('chat', 'could not remove empty session', …) with that sessionId.

[integration] When one listed session's readMeta throws SESSION_META_UNREADABLE, listSessions() returns the other rows and logs warn('chat', 'skipping unreadable session metadata', …) with that sessionId.

[integration] When a storage fake lacks removeMeta while the host closes a turnless session with empty history and no send attempts, close resolves and logger.warn('chat', 'could not remove empty session', { sessionId, cause }) records the removal failure.

[integration] When storage.removeMeta throws while replace leaves a turnless empty unsent session for a different id, the replacement continues and logger.warn('chat', 'could not remove empty session', { sessionId, cause }) records the left session's failure.
[integration] When the cleanup meta re-read returns null, removeIfEmpty removes nothing and logs nothing.

routing.reasoning: Session lifecycle cleanup, immutable history exposure, paginated filtering, lock-sensitive reopens and fault-tolerant teardown cross several modules under a tight host-size constraint. Session persistence/removal triggers the strict sessions security override.

suggestedCriteria: When a first send attempt throws before metadata persistence and the host closes, the session's meta is retained with updatedAt:null.
When switchTo changes only the model of an unsent empty session, storage.removeMeta is not called during that same-id switch.
When only turnless sessions are stored, resume({}) throws CHAT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND with the existing no-resumable-session message.
When resumable rows span multiple storage pages, listSessions returns every eligible row in the storage's original newest-first order, preserving heldByPid for a live-held eligible session.
After a completed live send on an already open session, host.history() continues to return the original opening snapshot rather than appended live messages.
When listSessions encounters a readMeta error other than SESSION_META_UNREADABLE, it rejects with that error rather than silently skipping the row.

modifiedFiles.reason: re-export `ChatHistory` from the chat barrel so the TUI replay imports it through it.

AC-5 lists the host's own freshly started session and expects it back with `heldByPid: 4242`; the list now excludes the host's own session, so the test resumes or stores a separate session with a recorded turn (`updatedAt` set) and asserts that row carries `heldByPid: 4242`.
assertions that compare the whole returned handle gain the new `history` field (`{ messages: [] }` for a new session).

userStories.title: Replay stored conversations as bounded transcript rows
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a pure replayHistory mapper that renders stored conversation text and completed one-line tool cards without thinking or unbounded tool data.

**Motivation** — Choosing a session swapped the host's session (`resumeSession`), but the transcript kept the welcome card only: `ChatApp` never reads the stored conversation, and `ChatHost` has no way to give it one.

**Approach** — A pure `replayHistory` maps stored messages to `TranscriptEntry` rows, mirroring nax-agent-acp's `replayTranscript` (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/translate/replay.ts`): tool inputs through `displayToolInput`, results through `toolResultPreview`, so a replay never shows more than the live turn did. This story implements the mapper only; US-004 wires it to ChatApp.

New pure `replayHistory(history)` in `packages/nax/src/tui/chat/history-replay.ts` implementing the replay mapping table below.

Replay mapping (`replayHistory`):
| Stored message | Entries |
|:--|:--|
| user, content starts with `COMPACTION_SUMMARY_PREFIX` | one `{ kind: "notice", text: "earlier conversation compacted" }` |
| user, content starts with `<skill name="X"` | one `{ kind: "user", text: "/X" }`, or `"/X <args>"` where args is the text after the LAST `</skill>\n\n` in the content, trimmed (a skill body may itself contain `</skill>`; production args carry a leading space); content that ends in `</skill>` has no args |
| user, any other non-empty content | one `{ kind: "user", text: content }` |
| user, empty content | none |
| assistant, non-empty content | one `{ kind: "reply", turnId: "history-<i>", text: content }` (`i` = message index) |
| assistant `toolCalls[j]` | one `{ kind: "tool", turnId: "history-<i>", callId, name, input: displayToolInput(input), status, preview, startedAt: savedAt, endedAt: savedAt, children: [] }` after the reply |
| assistant `thinking` | none |
| tool-result | none of its own; it sets the status and preview of the call with the same id |

A call whose result is present takes `status: "ok"` (or `"error"` when `isError`) and `preview: toolResultPreview(content)`; a call with no stored result takes `status: "error"` and `preview: "No result was recorded for this call."`. `startedAt`/`endedAt` take `savedAt`, or `"1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"` when `savedAt` is absent, so a replayed card never renders as running.

`TranscriptDoc` (`@nathapp/nax-agent`, type export) — `{ savedAt: string; messages: readonly ConversationMessage[]; … }`; a message is `{ role: "user"; content }`, `{ role: "assistant"; content; toolCalls?: { id; name; input }[]; thinking? }` or `{ role: "tool-result"; toolCallId; content; isError? }`.

`displayToolInput(input: unknown): unknown` and `toolResultPreview(content: string): string` (`@nathapp/nax-agent`, value exports) — the masking and caps the live `tool_call` / `tool_result` events get. `COMPACTION_SUMMARY_PREFIX` (`@nathapp/nax-agent/internal`) — a compacted transcript keeps the summary as a user message whose content starts with this prefix. `buildSkillInvocationMessage({ skill, args })` in `packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/skills-builder/index.ts` — the envelope is `<skill name="<qualifiedName>" location="<path>">`, a references line, the body, `</skill>`, then `\n\n<args>` when args are non-empty.

Index tool results by call id before mapping, following the read-only ACP reference's association pattern; do not copy its thinking replay. Apply the terminal-</skill> no-args rule before searching for the last delimiter, so a body containing its own closing marker and blank line cannot be mistaken for arguments. Preserve input order and original message indexes for history ids. Import ChatHistory through @/chat and consume the existing TranscriptEntry union rather than adding a second renderer/model.

Failure handling: a stored message has a role the mapping does not name — it is skipped; replay continues with the next message. A tool call's input cannot be displayed — `displayToolInput` already returns its bounded placeholder; replay uses it as the input.

**Scope** — In: create history-replay.ts and its mirrored unit tests, consuming US-002's ChatHistory snapshot and existing nax-agent helpers. Out: title persistence/list hygiene (US-001/US-002), mounting the replay or naming the header (US-004). Replaying a catalog command turn as the command the user typed: the transcript stores only the expanded template text, which is what replay shows. Replaying thinking blocks, and replaying nested subagent calls as children of their agent card. Showing per-call durations on replayed tool cards. Collapsing a skill invocation into an expandable row, live or replayed, belongs to the later chat-transcript-polish feature; this feature only replays a skill envelope as its typed `/name args` line. Any change to `@nathapp/nax-agent` or `@nathapp/nax-agent-acp`.

**Interface**
```typescript
replayHistory(history: ChatHistory): readonly TranscriptEntry[]
displayToolInput(input: unknown): unknown
toolResultPreview(content: string): string
```
The latter two signatures are existing upstream exports, not new implementations. Use the ChatHistory contract created by US-002; no live host, disk access or UI effects belong in replayHistory.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] replayHistory({ messages: [] }) returns an empty array.
[unit] A user message 'hello' replays as [{ kind: 'user', text: 'hello' }].
[unit] A user message with empty content replays as no entries.

[unit] A user message whose content is buildSkillInvocationMessage output for skill superpowers:brainstorming with args 'plan it' replays as { kind: 'user', text: '/superpowers:brainstorming plan it' }.
[unit] The same skill envelope with empty args replays as { kind: 'user', text: '/superpowers:brainstorming' }.
[unit] A skill envelope built with args ' plan it' (leading space, as /skill plan it produces) replays as { kind: 'user', text: '/superpowers:brainstorming plan it' }.
[unit] A skill envelope whose body itself contains the line </skill> and whose args are 'go' replays as { kind: 'user', text: '/superpowers:brainstorming go' }.
[unit] A skill envelope whose body contains </skill> followed by a blank line and more, built with empty args, replays as { kind: 'user', text: '/superpowers:brainstorming' }.
[unit] A user message starting with COMPACTION_SUMMARY_PREFIX replays as { kind: 'notice', text: 'earlier conversation compacted' }.
[unit] An assistant message at index 3 with content 'done' and no tool calls replays as { kind: 'reply', turnId: 'history-3', text: 'done' }.
[unit] An assistant message with empty content and one tool call replays as exactly one tool entry and no reply entry.

[unit] An assistant tool call { id: 'c1', name: 'Read', input: { path: 'a' } } followed by tool-result { toolCallId: 'c1', content: '17 lines' } replays as a tool entry with status: 'ok', preview equal to toolResultPreview('17 lines'), input equal to displayToolInput({ path: 'a' }), and children: [].
[unit] A tool-result with isError: true gives its call status: 'error'.
[unit] A tool call with no matching tool-result replays with status: 'error' and preview: 'No result was recorded for this call.'.
[unit] With savedAt: '2026-10-28T01:00:00.000Z', every replayed tool entry has startedAt and endedAt equal to it.
[unit] With savedAt absent, replayed tool entries have startedAt and endedAt equal to '1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'.
[unit] An assistant message's thinking blocks produce no entries.
[unit] A message whose role is not user, assistant or tool-result is skipped and the messages after it still replay.
[unit] A tool result whose content holds an sk- style secret replays with the masked preview toolResultPreview returns, not the raw content.
[unit] When a stored tool input cannot be displayed, replayHistory uses the bounded placeholder returned by displayToolInput as the replayed tool entry's input.

routing.reasoning: A pure mapper and mirrored tests use existing types and display helpers with a clear result-indexing algorithm. Although structurally medium, stored-session replay and credential masking require the strict sessions/security test strategy.

suggestedCriteria: Given an assistant message containing text and multiple tool calls, replayHistory returns the reply before the tool entries and preserves the calls' stored order.
When replayHistory receives an unmatched standalone tool-result, it produces no entry for that result.
When replayHistory processes frozen history messages and tool input, the original messages and inputs remain unchanged.

userStories.title: Rebuild resumed transcripts and name the active session
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Rebuild the visible conversation when the active session id changes and show its readable title in the header and resumed notice.

**Motivation** — The header (`headerLines`, `packages/nax/src/tui/chat/chat-status.ts`) shows product, version, model and mode, never the session.

**Approach** — Replay in the screen. `ChatApp` rebuilds its transcript whenever the session id changes (startup `--resume`, the picker, `/resume <id>`, `/clear`), and the header gains the session title. Consume the pure replayHistory mapper created by US-003; do not implement a parallel replay path.

Screen behaviour on a session change:
`ChatApp` keys its transcript on `host.current().sessionId`. On the first render (the initial state) and, through a layout effect declared before the notice effects, whenever the id changes, it sets the transcript to `[welcomeEntry(host), ...replayHistory(host.history?.() ?? { messages: [] }), notice]`, where `notice` is `{ kind: "notice", text: "resumed <sessionTitleText>" }` only when the replayed list is non-empty. Mode and model switches reopen the same id and leave the transcript alone. The `host.notice()` effect re-runs on a session id change as well as on a changed notice text, so resuming two interrupted sessions in a row shows the interrupted notice after each rebuild. Entries the other mount effects append (resource notice, sandbox warning, `host.notice()`) land after the rebuilt list, never before it.

The header's first line becomes `✻ nax chat v<version> · <model> · <mode> · <title>` when `meta.title` is non-null, with the title rendered by `sessionTitleText` and elided at the end with the theme's ellipsis (a new end-elision helper beside `elideMiddle`) so the line fits the header width. When fewer than 8 columns remain for the title text after the model, the mode and the ` · ` separator before the title, the title segment is left out entirely. The title is the first thing on the line to yield; product, version, model and mode are drawn as today.

`headerTitleLine` (`packages/nax/src/tui/chat/chat-status.ts`) — Target: `headerTitleLine(state, version, width, glyphs)`; `headerLines` passes its resolved width. `headerLines`' own input shape is unchanged. Use existing single-row sanitization and display-column measurement, not string length; use the theme's actual ellipsis and measure the whole existing prefix before reserving title space. Do not truncate the existing prefix differently to make room for a title.

`ChatApp` rebuilds its transcript from `host.history()` on the first render and on every session id change (a layout effect declared before the notice effects), ending with a `resumed <title>` notice when there is history; the header's first line shows the session title. Ensure /clear and picker completion share the same session-id transition mechanism. The first-render initializer and subsequent rebuild must not erase notices appended by other mount effects or reset same-id live entries.

routing.reasoning: Session-id keyed React state rebuilds, first-render history, layout/passive effect ordering, multiple resume entry points and display-width-aware headers cross UI seams. Session history handling invokes the strict sessions security override.

suggestedCriteria: When a model switch reopens the same session id, ChatApp retains its existing transcript rows without replaying or adding another resumed notice.
When the only stored messages are thinking blocks or empty content and replayHistory returns no entries, ChatApp omits the resumed notice.
When a full-mode unavailable-sandbox host mounts with stored history, its sandbox warning appears after the replayed rows and resumed notice.
When a header title contains wide Unicode characters, its elided title segment keeps the combined line within its available display-column budget.
When a header uses ASCII theme glyphs and a title needs truncation, its final title text ends with that theme's ellipsis.
